text:
julia: Heads up — our eval runner is flaking on the q4f quantized Llama variant. Same seed + same prompt but different outputs across workers.
ben: I can repro a small % locally. CI shows `pytest eval_runner::test_repro -k sampling` failing sporadically (about 3%).
anya: Do we have a minimal log? is it divergence at token 1 or later?
julia: Divergence at token 3-5 usually. I dumped the logits and rng call counts. Looks like the order of RNG consumption isn't stable when we mix streaming + prefix cache.
devon: That screams "sampler handoff". When streaming switches from cached prefix to live sampling we interleave sampler code paths. Some paths call into quantized kernels that internally consume RNG (curand?)
mat: Quantized attention kernels end up using fused ops — different kernel launches change the consume-order of random uniforms. If the global RNG is shared, sequence varies by microbatch ordering.
grace: Also noticed top_p uses a sort+cumprob codepath. On float16 the tie-breaker ordering isn't stable between CUDA kernels which can change how many tokens are included in the nucleus, which changes RNG draws.
ci-bot: Build #4921 failed on eval-runner sampling tests. Rerun triggered: flaky failure recorded. https://ci.internal/runs/4921
ben: I pushed a quick instrumented run: added a per-eval counter for RNG draws. When two workers shuffle microbatch order we get different counts even before divergence.
anya: Two immediate mitigations: 1) centralize RNG per-eval (single stream) so kernel internals draw from a provided buffer; 2) make top_p deterministic by enforcing stable sort / tie-breaker.
julia: Agree. Short term for CI: enable a deterministic-mode flag that seeds a per-eval PRNG and forces sampling to pull from that. It'll make tests reproducible even if kernels are nondet.
mat: Example pattern (toy):
```
# per-eval generator
gen = torch.Generator(device='cpu')
gen.manual_seed(base_seed ^ eval_id)
# wrapper used by samplers/kernels
def rand_uniform(n):
    return torch.rand(n, generator=gen, device='cpu')
```
But note: that forces host-side draws and may slow down high-throughput paths.
devon: For perf-critical path we can pre-generate chunks on cpu then upload contiguous tensors to device so kernels consume from a deterministic buffer without invoking their own RNG.
ben: I'll prototype a seeded buffer approach. If it solves CI flake we can gate behind `--deterministic-evals` in tests.
grace: Also file an issue to harden top_p: stable sort by (prob, token_id) and avoid reducer-level nondet ops.
anya: Tests to add: reproduce with 2-worker interleaving (shuffle microbatch), with q4f quant kernels, and assert token-level equality for fixed seed under deterministic-mode.
julia: Action items:
- ben: prototype seeded buffer + small perf test (owner)
- mat: PR for stable top_p sort and add tie-breaker (owner)
- devon: add CI config to run deterministic-mode for the sampling test (owner)
- grace: open issue documenting kernel RNG calls and quant kernels that rely on curand (owner)
I'll open the umbrella PR that flips the flag in CI once prototypes land.
ben: ack
ci-bot: Created ticket INF-1187 for tracking flaky eval sampling.
julia: Thanks — if anyone has a repro with exact commands please paste them here. I attached logs to INF-1187.
